text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000109 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation across every complexity stratum, including many 0-1 condition patients, but the very small documented sample does not show unsupported billing.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not confined to complex patients: in each condition-count stratum this provider's 99215 share runs roughly three times the all-provider share, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include patients with only nonspecific diagnoses such as abdominal pain, rash, URI or follow-up codes (e.g., C0054183, C0055547, C0056064, C0054427), a pattern consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. Against that, the six documented 99215 claims all supported high MDM with time recorded in the mid-40-minute range (e.g., C0054968, C0055534), and the only below-billed finding was a single 99214 (C0054733). Six charts out of 422 99215 claims is far too thin to clear the pattern, and the 3 notes claiming moderate-plus data review without any lab or test line on the claim are weak signs that some documentation may be templated or inflated. A reviewer should first request records specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and check whether their MDM and time genuinely reflect high complexity, and should look for cloned note language across the supported 99215 charts."}
